_comment: The numbers the prediction figures print, as data rather than as pixels inside a PNG.
Before this file they existed only in the images. Nothing in the repo would have noticed the
checkpoint drifting away from what the front page claimed -- tests/test_scripts_local.py
asserts only that shift is 0-12 ppm and J is 0-30 Hz.
Two tests use this. tests/test_figure_numbers.py (unit, no checkpoint, runs in CI) ties the
committed SVG's table to this file. tests/test_scripts_local.py (model tier, skip-gated) ties
this file to the checkpoint. The second one SKIPS in CI, so it can never catch data-vs-
checkpoint drift there -- read the skip count, do not read a green suite as evidence about it.

provenance.checkpoint_md5_source: scripts/download_weights.py EXPECTED_MD5 -- verified equal to the local file
note: Both figures were measured in ONE process against ONE checkpoint. roi_S10 reproduced the
committed PNG exactly, every field. roi_S8 reproduced none of it beyond an approximate
delta. That pairing excludes environment drift as the explanation: a version-dependent
decoder assignment would have to disturb both.
The superseded example_prediction_vanillin.png printed GROUND-TRUTH delta (7.420 / 7.385 /
6.959 -- the hardcoded ASSIGNMENTS of scripts/gen_molecule_figure.py, deleted in 2827cdb)
in a column captioned as a prediction, while example_prediction.png printed predicted
delta. Both now print predicted delta, which is what makes the caption's 'the predictions
reproduce the ground truth' claim checkable rather than circular.
Its max J was additionally transposed between the two ~8 Hz ortho protons, which was
invisible because ground truth carries 8.1 twice -- H5 and H6 share one physical coupling,
so the published comparison read as a good match in either order.

example_prediction.alt: MolDeTr detects three aromatic 1H multiplets of guajazulene at 500 MHz; the assignment table lists proton count, chemical shift in ppm, largest coupling max J in Hz, and line width for each

example_prediction_vanillin.alt: MolDeTr detects the three aromatic protons of vanillin at 300 MHz as a classic ABX pattern; the assignment table lists proton count, chemical shift, largest coupling, and line width for each
